translation:
Betony
Betony

The herb betony breaks up the aforementioned tumors and is blessed with wine; it is good taken as an elixir, and its leaves, described below, and the juice is good for pains and ailments of the months, given with red oil while the juice remains fresh; with wine it is good for coughs and tightness of the chest. The powder, mixed or drunk with wine, softens the belly. Applied to the face, the raw leaf draws out tears and stops bleeding; also its leaf, crushed with salt and spread on sores that arise like a plaster, relieves them; it also cures swellings; and placed on a bite from a snake, it heals immediately.

The herb of Saturn is very useful for pain of the belly and for swollen feet. For one who suffers pain of the feet, let them eat the cooked root and the said herb, and they will be relieved. translation:
Greater Centaury                    Lesser Centaury

The herb greater centaury has virtue against the bite of [serpents] — it keeps the bite at bay and frees [the victim]. It removes blemishes: take its juice in rose oil, place it in the eye, and it eats away the clouding and reveals the light. It is also good cooked; the turnip-root removes [deposits from] the earth and causes the hair to grow. It grows in hard, firm, and rocky places and has many virtues.

This [plant] cures hemorrhoids, purges [bad] humors, and kills hemorrhoids. Take the juice of the vine and it removes roughness from the eyes. On the 25th day of the month of March and throughout the year, apply it. The dried juice, powdered and placed in the eye, erodes the cloudiness and clears the sight. Given as a drink with green wine, it kills worms of the belly, and has many other virtues. It grows in sandy and firm soils.

The eagle, they say, when it wishes to look upon the heights, desires to behold the king of nature. translation:
Licorice.

The herb licorice grows in coastal plains; it is found in the lowland of Grosseto, on the marina of Siena, in great abundance. It is good for catarrh and all chest ailments. Prepare it in this way: take the root of this herb, then hyssop, and add figs and raisins for months. Add cubeb and [illegible], and fennel root, and tiny roots of [illegible]. And honey. And [illegible] and barley water, and make a syrup. Add honey and mix everything together and strain it. Give this syrup to drink 6 times — in the evening and in the morning. This syrup purges the body and in this way cures the illness of catarrh and of plague and of the chest. It is also good for nausea and for abscesses caused by cold, and for sudden fever it brings relief. The doctor notes it has many good virtues for the human body. It is gathered in May and [illegible], and at every season it is found and is good.

description: 180 botanical illustrations with human-faced mandrake. Medieval meets Renaissance botanical art.
translation:
Herb mandrake female

Mandrake, Female.

The herb mandrake female grows in mountainous places, in rocky meadows and fields, and those who gather it come to its smell from afar, and it stands from a distance, and its virtue is great among plants, and its spirit among the stones kills instantly as if by lightning. This mandrake, gather its root, which is good to give to eat to a woman who, because of a cold condition — I say because of colic — cannot conceive children. Know that this root will gladden every pregnant woman who carries female children, and the living creature will last as long as she has the root and no more. The leaves and seeds are good, and their juice is good for every blemish of the eye, and it cleans away and removes what grows around it; and if it were to burn the light in a lantern, and so its form, which is made in the likeness of a woman — whoever carries it on their person will have the love of all women, and all those who see it will grant every honor and grace and make themselves obedient to that person. And tell this to a sign of birth and carry it with you to the doctor. The firm one has the power to make things good and reliable. A miraculous herb. Its virtues: the little one of the same and its essence.

translation:
Male Mandrake herb

The mandrake herb (male): there are two varieties, male and female. The male is coarser and the female is more like lettuce, and is more powerful. Use the female. It is good for pain, plague, and pestilence — place it in oil for two days, then every morning bring it to light in clear air. Also, the leaf placed on any wound defends against and frees from [illegible]. Juice mixed with honey, applied to the chest, draws out every abscess and other humors — something almost impossible to believe. Know that when you go to collect it, do not turn your head away, otherwise it will disappear, and once gone you will never see it again. And when you dig it up, if you do not cut it, tie the root to a dog's feet — it has a long [root] — and do not listen to the noise; cover your ears. And know that this pestilence goes and drives away evil spirits, and immediately you would die [if exposed improperly]. Take care. And know that it has many virtues — this root, and if carried on the person, no one can harm you or approach you — every evil man flees from one who carries it, so be safe from every evil spirit. The doctor confirms this. At 45 [conditions/uses] and medicines.

description: 180 botanical illustrations with human-faced mandrake. Medieval meets Renaissance botanical art.
translation:
263

Herb Rhubarb

The herb rhubarb grows among the Saracens and in those parts of the Orient. The first reason why this herb is called rhubarb is because it grows outside the bark of a tree, and therefore it is called rhubarb. The second reason is that it grows in Barbary, in the land of the Berbers. The third reason why it is called reobarbaros is that it is the sovereign of all other medicines and herbs, for nothing can compare to this rhubarb — that is, it is the best of all other purgatives, and therefore it enters into many electuaries, purgatives, and spice preparations, which are difficult for physicians to dispense with. This then is the flower of every medicine. The doctor recommends it in matters of medicine according to his prescription. Physicians of Barbary call it "figo reobarbaros," and it is by nature of greater substance than a fungus.

The herb bracken: take an iron tool, a wood spine, and place the flesh of the leaf, ground 2 or 3 times, and squeeze it out: and it becomes like a little bundle, a certain companion [remedy]. Take the root and pound it and mix it into a paste and give it to drink — it will quickly heal. It grows on mountains in sunny spots, and is found on mountains and in shaded glens.

Bracken Minor

The herb bracken minor is good for headache — place it upon the head; also for the heat of the Sun, do not let it go to the head. The eagle, when it goes up high, uses it to preserve its sight. It grows on alpine mountains and is found in great abundance there.

translation:
Lucia Major (Greater Lucia)

The herb Lucia Major grows in rocky places and in moist, shaded locations — it is an herb of the lily family. It is an ornament of fish [or: a plant decorated with fish markings].

It is called by names... [partial/fragmentary]

The second [property]: it makes the night bright like a star.
The third: each of its leaves has eyes of blue-violet color on a red background, and those that glow at night — their juice, when applied to the eye with a cloth compress, ten times over, gently illuminates every body applied to it. The interior gives light. It also heals every wound when pounded alone. It produces a kind of oil [when prepared with certain herbs].

It also, when a [bird or creature] is about to be born and cannot come out easily, helps the birth; placed inside the nest it gives the creature four [things] by which it can be nourished. It makes itself invisible. It heals wounds in a wondrous way. Take it, treat it, and bind it around the nest with the bones of the young. Pound it into small pieces and restore the [creature] with the juice of the herbs of Borzini — the wound will be as it was before, made whole again.

Also, take the fresh leaf, which belongs to the planet Jupiter, and pound it finely as described above — all the birds that are called [by this herb's name] will be drawn to it. Furthermore, it causes [something] to be born rather than to flee.

                              ambra

The herb Regina comes in 3 varieties and is a wondrous herb — whoever carries it on their person will never be seen. It grows in many rocky and dry places; it is found there and also in mountain alpine areas, and it is a small herb, one finger's height from the ground or less, and has yellow flowers.   The herb Aralea maior:
ariscola, zdirito, istiparmo, congio, orto, prischala, feraria — whoever
carries it on themselves, dried, drives away thieves and serpents, and one need not fear them; he is safe from every enemy. But first have a Mass said over it, and gather it at the crescent moon in the sign of Taurus, and then keep it wrapped in a white cloth. And do not sin with it in the sin of lust. The juice mixed with milk removes subtle spells; mixed with honey it purifies the body. It grows in marshy, mountain, and rocky places and has a good fragrance like sweet-smelling honey.

The herb oregano, powdered and boiled in hot water, relieves the discomfort of a bite — that is, the burning of the stomach — [illegible] and stops it.

The herb oregano is hot and dry in its degree. It has many uses. Cooked and given to drink, it is good for those who have taken poison, or for one who has been bitten by a viper or a rabid dog; drunk, it is good for driving out the poison and other venoms within the body. Also the juice, drunk, is good for pains, whether from bruising or beating or for another reason. Furthermore, the juice is good to give to drink for tropical ailments and to clear out their humors and bruising. And its root, gathered at the waxing moon [followed by abbreviated/formulaic dosage and preparation notes largely illegible]. It is proven that whoever carries this herb on their person, no evil, no harm, no spirit, nor shadow can trouble any house where it is kept.

translation:
The first type of lunar herb, the second type of lunar grass, the third type of rounded lunar herb.

First variety               Second variety               Third variety

The lunar herb [and its properties] and how it spreads and its species and kinds. These are all good for multiplying gold and silver. Take the fine powder of these lunar herbs, then put the powder into the vessel with the silver and it will cause it to grow and increase, or with gold, as much powder as you put in of these herbs will cause it to increase and grow finer in the vessel or burn. The powder from the said [herb] gives six times the weight in gold in florins. And in this way, grind the herb and mix it. Anoint with it a portion of gold and take the powder of these lunar herbs, two parts [measure], apply it to multiply and preserve; and take one pound of powder of the herb called the olive-like lunar herb, separated and filtered, two pounds, of silver or gold without impurity. These lunar herbs are not found in many places — in mountainous areas, in the hills, and in the meadows, in sandy non-marshy ground; they grow well toward June or thereabouts. And also the azure lunar herb grows in the hills. The coastal hills are not marshy but are sandy terrain near the sea.

Lunar globosa [Globe Moonwort]

The herb lunaria and its kind come in two varieties: this one is the better one, with leaves that are green on top and somewhat reddish below; the little buds are green. This herb grows in every kind of terrain. And one [stalk] spreads and extends further. Some say it is the greater lunaria. It grows and thrives and ends [its season]. And it grows in many hollows and in many other places.

translation:
Aristolochia longa                    Aristolochia rotunda

[illustration left]                      [illustration right]

The herb Aristolochia rotunda is good: the root powdered with honey, given for paralysis, used for forty days of fasting. Burn the leaf and receive the smoke — it drives away demons from the house and liberates. Also, carrying it on one's person keeps snakes away so they will not bite you. It has many virtues for the ailments of the home [remainder illegible].

Herb Aristolochia longa. For the ailment of catarrh [and domestic ailments, illegible]: the root cooked under the ashes [in the manner described], take it [illegible], with salt and oil for [illegible] days. [Illegible] remedy. And it liberates quickly. The juice of the ripe seed, taken [illegible] with wine, washes the member where the itching was, and quickly liberates it. For the burning, apply the juice of the leaves; spread it [on the affected area] and it immediately takes away the burning. It has many virtues: night cramps, and those who are tender and delicate — it is found from August until October. Also, for one who is paralyzed, use the root with eggs.

translation:
Bryony, also called Golidana, or Wild Bryony / Colombine:

The herb Bryony has many names. There are those who say it removes and draws out [toxins], and boiling it helps the body rise from its condition, and then it is applied after [to the affected area] for cramps and similar complaints. And in an ointment it heals. And if one takes some of the root and gives a portion of it [as a remedy], along with other preparations and decoctions made from it, it will cause the body to purge — all this being at the discretion of the physician according to the patient's constitution and condition.
